opps.title: Montauk — 10% of your commission, down 10% YoY

opps.title: 2 accounts stopped ordering — $449 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Barcade_2, was worth 357 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: 4 brands with real placement gaps — 231 open doors
opps.body: These brands land in far more accounts like yours than they do in your book. The comparison is not raw company share: it weights each brand's on- and off-premise placement rate by your own channel mix, so an on-premise book is never judged against a supermarket brand's reach. Each door below is valued at what a typical account doing business in that brand actually buys company-wide (the median, not an average), scaled down to the size of the doors you actually call on — so these are ordinary placements in YOUR kind of account, not best-case ones in someone else's. Closing every gap would be worth roughly $11,256 — that is a ceiling, not a forecast, and it compares against $40,234 of commission in your book today. Take the top one or two lines; the whole list is not a year's work.

opps.title: 2 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 148 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 148 cases and about $148 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.
